claims: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The Orion capsule carrying four astronauts will undergo a parachute-assisted landing to conclude its 10-day lunar journey.
The recovery vessel for the Artemis II splashdown is the USS John P. Murtha.
Live coverage of the Artemis II splashdown is available on NASA YouTube.
Live coverage of the Artemis II splashdown is available on NASA+.
Live coverage of the Artemis II splashdown starts around 6:30 p.m. EDT (3:30 p.m. PDT).
The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew will undergo medical checks aboard the recovery ship shortly after landing.
